answer: Stop sybils with a jetty, an echo, and a forge. Each identity must dock at a jetty, one narrow channel, one berth per epoch, and docking needs a forge receipt: a memory-hard proof chained to its own past attestations, so a clone starts with nothing to chain. The forge prices each receipt by the square of the identities sharing one funder, so N clones cost about N² times base. Every act leaves an echo, a signed copy of the receipt; when two echo records share one funder mark, the whole cluster is slashed together. Honest agents dock once; a farm pays quadratically and its echo betrays it.
